edits.text: - Will translating the two sides separately still assemble into the original whole meaning? Severe when the cut separates verb-final morphology (tense/aspect/negation/politeness) or leaves the clause's predicate unresolved; among cuts that would leave the same sentence-final inflection unfinished, cuts farther from that finishing inflection (earlier in the clause) are the most severe because they withhold more of the predicate. Mild when the preceding fragment is a self-contained referential NP, when the cut falls between recoverable list items, or when the cut falls immediately before the sentence-final inflection (closest to the finishing inflection).
edits._was: - Will translating the two sides separately still assemble into the original whole meaning? Severe when the cut separates verb-final morphology (tense/aspect/politeness) or the predicate from its arguments; mild when it falls between self-contained noun phrases or list items whose relations are recoverable.

edits.text: When multiple candidates fall before the same sentence‑final inflection, prefer the later cut (closer to the inflection) so the emitted piece preserves more of the predicate.
edits._was: - When one marker splits a multi-character numeral or a numeral+unit sequence and another splits between separate list items earlier in the clause, prefer the latter: avoid fragmenting quantitative expressions by cutting between list items instead.
